chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Yahya al-Wasiti, from Ismail al-Basri, from Zurara ibn A'yan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the rubbing (of the penis). He said: He is having sex with himself, there is nothing upon it.

key_terms.الدَّلْكِ: Rubbing (specifically of the penis to induce ejaculation)
key_terms.لَا شَيْءَ عَلَيْهِ: There is nothing upon him (no penalty due)
key_terms.نَاكِحُ نَفْسِهِ: He is having sex with himself (a metaphorical legal classification)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on male masturbation regarding financial penalties?
ai.summary: In this concise ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the term 'ad-dalk' (rubbing) is interpreted as a form of self-intimacy, categorizing it as 'having sex with oneself.' The Imam specifies that this act incurs no financial penalty (kaffarah or diyyah), distinguishing it from other sexual transgressions that might require compensation, thereby clarifying its legal status within Shia jurisprudence. This hadith is frequently cited in discussions of *al-dalk* to establish that while it may be disliked or prohibited depending on the school of thought, it does not carry the specific monetary fines associated with other illicit sexual acts.

en.hubeali:
Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abu Yahya Al Wasity, from Ismail Al Basry, from Zurara Bin Ayn, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the rubbing (the manhood). He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He is having sex with himself, there is nothing upon it’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ahmad ibn Muhammad from has narrated from abu Yahya al-Wasitiy from ‘Isma’il al-Basriy from Zurarah ibn ’A‘yun who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about one’s playing to cause his semen to discharge.
He (the Imam) said, ‘He is like going to bed with himself and there is no punishment on him (but it is like fornication as regards to sinfulness).”’
